name: Bashama ibn Hazn al-Nahshali
bio: Bashama ibn Hazn was a poet of the Nahshal clan of Darim, part of the tribe of Tamim, of whom almost nothing is known. Al-Amidi lists him in his dictionary of poets' names without any further lineage and quotes five lines of his poem “We, the sons of Nahshal”; al-Marzuqi's commentary on the Hamasa calls him Bashama ibn Jaz', and al-Shantamari says Ibn Hazn is the more correct form. Al-Baghdadi found no biography of him and thought him a poet of the Islamic period, since al-Mubarrad traces some of the poem's ideas to Islamic poets such as Ka'b ibn Malik and al-Qattal al-Kilabi, while the commentary on the Hamasa ascribed to Abu al-Ala al-Ma'arri marks him pre-Islamic; al-Zirikli's al-A'lam has no entry for him. Al-Jahiz quotes other lines of his, praising herdsmen who fought with their staffs at a watering place. He is known for the Hamasa poem “We greet you, Salma, so greet us”, whose authorship is much disputed: al-Baghdadi judged it his, and a note in one manuscript of al-Mubarrad's al-Kamil identifies him with the Abu Makhzum al-Nahshali to whom al-Mubarrad gives it.
